evidence: sql_threads.py:151-159 wraps slot.acquire() in asyncio.timeout and catches TimeoutError. Read stdlib 3.11.16 and 3.12.13 asyncio/timeouts.py: Timeout.__aexit__ (3.12 l.97-119; 3.11 l.112-115) calls task.uncancel() and raises builtin TimeoutError from the CancelledError when state is EXPIRING and no other cancel is pending. In 3.11 asyncio.TimeoutError is the builtin. Slot leak: Semaphore.acquire (locks.py 3.12 l.363-397; 3.11 l.364-398) on CancelledError does 'if not fut.cancelled(): self._value += 1; self._wake_up_next()'. _wake_up_next decrements _value when it sets the waiter result (l.413-417), so a waiter granted a slot in the same tick as the timeout cancel gets it returned. If fut itself was cancelled, no slot was ever taken. Absolute-claim input traced: grant (release -> set_result) in the same loop tick as the timeout's task.cancel(); the task is thrown CancelledError at 'await fut', fut not cancelled, value restored, then re-raised and converted to TimeoutError. The normal-return path has no await between acquire return and __aexit__, so the timeout cannot fire after the slot is held.

Read CPython 3.11.16 asyncio/tasks.py wait_for (lines 473-479): on CancelledError while awaiting waiter, `if fut.done(): return fut.result()` swallows the cancellation. wait_for(slot.acquire()) runs acquire in an inner task; if release() grants the slot (acquire's fut set, inner task completes) in the same tick the outer task is cancelled, wait_for returns True and the cancelled caller proceeds to run the SQL. Input traced: release() then task.cancel() before the loop runs the waiter. With asyncio.timeout + await slot.acquire() (sql_threads.py:152-153), the cancel is thrown directly into Semaphore.acquire; locks.py 3.11 lines 390-394: `except CancelledError: if not fut.cancelled(): self._value += 1; self._wake_up_next(); raise` re-releases the granted slot and re-raises, so the cancelled call does not run. The comment's claim and implication hold.

sql_threads.py:115-121: call_soon_threadsafe(slot.release) is wrapped in try/except RuntimeError. If loop.is_closed() the handler returns silently; otherwise it emits a single logger.error naming only type(exc).__name__ (not the message). CPython BaseEventLoop.call_soon_threadsafe calls _check_closed(), which raises RuntimeError('Event loop is closed'); _write_to_self swallows OSError, so no other exception type is raised by stdlib. loop.is_closed() just returns self._closed and cannot raise. Non-RuntimeError escapes would need a non-stdlib loop; none is used here, and concurrent.futures also catches and logs callback exceptions, so nothing propagates into the worker.

sql_threads.py:143-175. Rejection: TimeoutError from asyncio.timeout at 152-154 logs logger.warning unconditionally (155-158) then raises SqlWorkersBusyError before submit at 165; the throttle _warn_saturated (102-112) is only called at 148 and is separate, so the interval does not limit rejection logs. Cancellation: (a) slot granted and cancelled in same tick: asyncio.Semaphore.acquire catches CancelledError, restores the value if the waiter future was already granted, and re-raises, so the CancelledError propagates out of the timeout block (external cancel is not converted to TimeoutError) and never reaches submit; if it is the timeout that cancels in that tick, it becomes TimeoutError and still rejects without running. Cancellation after submit is the documented started-call case, not the claim. Absolute claim holds for both named inputs.

Test (tests/unit/test_sql_runner_event_loop.py:296-318) fills the pool with extra=0 (value 0, locked). The queued run_blocking_sql task, on the first sleep(0), sees slot.locked() (sql_threads.py:147), enters asyncio.timeout and awaits slot.acquire() (152-153); the other two sleeps are harmless. slot.release() then does _value+=1 and _wake_up_next, which sets the waiter result and decrements _value to 0 (locked still true). queued.cancel() finds the waiter future already done, so the task gets _must_cancel and CancelledError is thrown into Semaphore.acquire, whose except branch (fut not cancelled) does _value+=1 and _wake_up_next, then re-raises. That behaviour is the same on 3.11 and 3.12. So the caller is cancelled (asserted), the call never reaches submit (ran == [] asserted after holders finish), and not slot.locked() holds because the cancelled waiter returned its grant. Had the grant been kept, value would stay 0 and locked() would be True, so the assertion tells the fixed code from the buggy path. On the hint: the test's extra release leaves the semaphore at 1 after the cancel, so after holders finish it is 9, above SQL_WORKER_THREADS. The semaphore is per-loop (WeakKeyDictionary keyed by loop), so this is confined to that test's loop. The assertion reflects the waiter's returned slot, not the extra release alone, since the grant-without-return would give locked True.
